replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Math was always a struggle for me, even in school. I never really understood it, and it made me feel frustrated. I dropped out after lower secondary, so I never got a chance to improve. Now, I avoid it as much as possible—it’s not something I enjoy or see much use for in my daily life. My parents were educated in math-heavy fields, but I just never clicked with it.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Honestly, yes. Just the thought of trying to solve a math problem makes me feel uneasy. It brings back bad memories from school, and I worry I’ll never understand it. I try not to dwell on it, but it’s definitely a source of stress for me. I’d rather focus on things I’m better at, like history or art.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: No, I haven’t. Math isn’t something I’m interested in improving, so I never looked into AI tools for it. Even if I did, I doubt I’d trust myself to use them properly. I stick to what I know and avoid anything that feels too complicated or overwhelming. My kids use tablets for school stuff, but I stay out of it.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: I’m not sure I can explain it clearly—I barely remember how to do it myself. But from what I recall, you’d move terms around to isolate the variable, maybe factor it, and then solve for the roots. It’s all just symbols to me, and I’d likely mess it up. I’d rather let someone who understands it handle the math.

I don’t know how to do that. The idea of calculus makes my head spin. Stationary points? Sounds like something advanced, and I stopped learning math a long time ago. I’d need a lot of help just to understand what you’re even asking, let alone explain it. It’s not something I’ve ever tried to tackle.
replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: I have no idea what Principal Component Analysis is, and I’d be too anxious to even try learning it. Math like that is way beyond my comfort zone. I’d rather focus on simpler topics or just avoid it altogether. If you’re asking me to teach it, I’d need a lot of patience—and probably still fail.
replies.According to you, how can LLMs be used t: I don’t see how LLMs would help someone like me, but maybe they could simplify math for kids or beginners. If they could explain things in plain language, without all the confusing symbols, it might make a difference. For me, though, I’d still avoid it—I’m more of a visual learner, and math just doesn’t click that way.
